text:
alex: Quick heads-up — PR #4821 (runtime:kv-cache) is blocked until we get architecture review sign-off on the new sharding fallback in the RFC. RFC: https://rfc.redwood.ai/rfcs/312 (see section 4.2). cc @maria @devon

maria: Thanks, alex. I'll take a look today. Is there a minimal checklist you want me to verify?

alex: main things: 1) correctness of fallback routing logic, 2) perf regressions for short-seq (<=128), 3) compatibility with dedicated pools. Link to PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/-/merge_requests/4821 

devon: can you paste the snippet for the new routing policy? easier to eyeball here.

alex: sure:
```
policy {
  prefer: \"dedicated\"
  fallback_order: [\"hosted\", \"quantized-compat\"]
  latency_sla_ms: 50
}
```

sophia: re: perf — I kicked off the perf job, logs here: https://perf.redwood.ai/job/4821. baseline vs changes look fine for long seqs but short seq p50 +6ms. I'll add a note in the PR.

maria: read through RFC section 4.2.2. One question: the cached-prefix eviction could cause cold starts in dedicated pools — need explicit mitigation in the RFC or the PR should add a short-term guard (flag). I can approve the PR once that's addressed.

tj: @maria +1 on the mitigation ask. infra already prefers canary rollout for this kind of change. I can be approver after you ok.

alex: thanks. I'll add a feature-flag gate and a canary deployment plan to the PR by EOD.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline passed: unit, lint. Perf job queued by sophia.

maria: Verified feature-flag code + updated docs. left one tiny comment about log level.

devon: small nit in tests, pushed a fix.

maria: LGTM. Approving now. :thumbsup:

tj: Approving for infra safety.

alex: great — since RFC is already linked and maria approved architecture concerns, I'll merge tomorrow 09:00 PT and start a 6-hour canary. If any regressions, revert and rollback plan is in PR.

sophia: I'll monitor perf during canary.

alex: thanks all :rocket:
